$comment: All narrative text. Word budget ~1,200 at MVP; max two lines on screen. Proper nouns never explained. See design doc §6 for voice rules.

waystones.sunfield-meadow: Walk gently. The meadow fed them, too, and they are under it.
waystones.bramble-hedgerows: The stone does not grow back. Take it like you mean it.
waystones.old-growth-wood: These roots drink deeper than you will ever dig. Let them.
waystones.silverrun-river: The river keeps no ledger. Count what you take, for it will not.
waystones.mistfen-marsh: The fen remembers every weight it has carried. Step lightly; it is counting.
waystones.the-hollows: The dark below was not always empty. Leave it the quiet it paid for.
waystones.highland-crags: Others folded flocks on this height, and the wind has their names. Count yours home each night.

verses.sunfield-meadow: What you carry is borrowed. Set some down, and see what follows you home.
verses.bramble-hedgerows: Sweetness kept, stone made bright. Show the hedge what the taking taught you.
verses.old-growth-wood: Wood made useful, and one bone of what came before. The grove would hold it again.
verses.silverrun-river: Of all you pulled from the water, the river asks the finest back. It knows you have it.
verses.mistfen-marsh: Brew what the still water grew, and pour a little back where the lights gather.
verses.the-hollows: Ore made bright, and the glass the burning left. Carry the deep's own wealth back down.
verses.highland-crags: What the flock gives freely, give on. The warmth was never yours to keep.

provisioner.line: Sell me nothing you would weep to lose. I do not give refunds, and the land does not either.
The last warden asked fewer questions. Hm. Perhaps that was the trouble.

migrationVignette: The camp folds. The land exhales.

insectPlates.stags-herald: Antlers on a beetle no longer than your thumb. It fought something once, or meant to. The drawing is all I keep; the meadow keeps the rest.
insectPlates.silver-skimmer: It held the one reach of river all afternoon and let me sketch it, wings still. The river fed its kind ten thousand years. I gave the page my hand and gave the water back its guest.
insectPlates.those-who-sow: They carry the flowers from field to field without being asked, and have longer than we have. Whoever tends this place, it is not only us. I drew them, and let them go on.
insectPlates.lantern-bearers: They light the drowned paths every night, for no one. I was never the reason, and I may still be grateful. Four evenings of drawing, and not one lantern paused for me.
insectPlates.quiet-court: They sing in galleries no light has ever reached, to no audience at all. Five evenings by lamplight, drawing what has never been seen. They did not stop singing once.
insectPlates.parchment-wings: Wings thin as the pages I draw them on, and they fly only while the sun holds. Four afternoons of sun, this high, in this wind. I owed the mountain every one.
insectPlates.wayfarers-plate: A loose leaf, folded twice, left in a place I would pass. Another hand drew it, steadier than mine and long gone. I did not walk for this one. It is in the book now, and I am still walking.
